newsitem.title: UK: Parenthood creates traditional roles - British study.
newsitem.headline: Parenthood creates traditional roles - British study.

text.p: Babies bring more than sleepless nights to new parents -- they also throw them back into more traditional roles as husband and wife, British psychologists said on Tuesday.

Even the most progressive couples who share responsibility for earning a living and housework regress to old-fashioned roles once a baby is born, Gill Cappuccini and Ray Cochrane of Birmingham University said.
They studied 100 married couples expecting their first child. About two-thirds considered they had equal partnerships, holding down jobs and sharing housework, shopping and cooking.
But Cappuccini said this changed as soon as the baby was born and the mothers stayed home, either on maternity leave or a career break.
"In nearly all cases the man's career becomes more important after the birth," she told a conference of the British Psychological Society at Strathclyde University.

"Some of these people said what an unexpected shock it was when the baby arrived in the house. They try to make sense of a very new situation and find themselves adopting the old traditional roles," she added.
"The woman ends up spending most time with the baby and doing most of the housework."
Often the man sought promotion because of the added expense a child brings. "Soon this begins to affect everything else and life is never quite the same again."
Most of the couples, however, said they were happy with the new arrangements and rated marital satisfaction as high.
